title: Constraints on recovering quantum information after erasure
authors: Mohammad A. Alhejji, Noah Lordi, Omkar Baraskar, Ariel Shlosberg, Emanuel Knill
abstract: Suppose that we encode quantum information into $ n $ physical carriers. With what probabilities can we perfectly recover the quantum information after sets of carriers have been erased? This question arises in the study of quantum erasure channels, for which M.B. Hastings conjectured that if each carrier is independently erased with probability $ t \geq 1/2 $, then it is impossible to recover the quantum information with asymptotically vanishing error and probability $ > 1-t $. We prove this conjecture by establishing new no-cloning constraints on realizable recovery probabilities.
summary: This paper investigates the mathematical limits on recovering quantum information when some physical carriers are lost due to an erasure channel. By deriving constraints based on no-cloning principles and graph theory, it proves a major conjecture about these channels. The findings show that physical realizability imposes stricter limitations than simple combinatorial bounds for systems with five or more carriers.
main_problem: The paper determines the fundamental constraints on the probabilities with which quantum information can be perfectly recovered after arbitrary sets of physical carriers are erased.
main_result: It proves a conjecture regarding quantum erasure channels by establishing new no-cloning constraints, showing that for $n>4$, realizable recovery probabilities ($Q_n$) are strictly smaller than the set defined only by disjointness constraints ($T_n$).
method: The analysis combines concepts from quantum coding theory, graph theory (using Lovász numbers), and semidefinite programming (SDP) to derive necessary conditions for physical realizability.
model_or_system: The model involves encoding quantum information into $n$ physical carriers. The core mathematical object is the set $\mathcal{Q}_n$, which characterizes all possible probability tuples $(q_S)$ achievable by a quantum code under erasure channels.
key_observables: Recovery probabilities $q_S$; the Lovász number $\vartheta(G_F)$; and bounds on sums of these probabilities (e.g., $\sum q_{\{i,j\}} \le \sqrt{5}$ for $n=5$).
important_parameters: The number of carriers ($n$), the erasure probability ($t$), and the minimum distance ($d$) of the underlying quantum code.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on assuming the encoding channel is isometric (without loss of generality) and uses techniques like SDP to derive upper bounds based on physical constraints.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate circuits for composite quantum channels involving maximally entangled states, showing how recovery operations are modeled across multiple carriers.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the set $\mathcal{Q}_n$ and comparing it to a simpler set $\mathcal{T}_n$. It then derives constraints using graph theory (Lovász number) and finally proves results for small $n$, culminating in proving the erasure-simulation conjecture.
why_interesting: The work establishes fundamental, non-trivial bounds on quantum information processing capabilities under noise/erasure, which is crucial for designing robust quantum communication protocols.
